_readme: Per-run monitoring log, one file per calendar day (America/Phoenix), used to generate the Daily PDF Report. Distinct from cases.json, which is the permanent case/review-queue index.
_run_note: Fourth scheduled Mon-Fri run, and the first to include Redland Ranch Roses (added to the roster 2026-09-16). Product-count deltas since 2026-09-16: Muse Roses 750->751, Rose Explosion 1414->1416 (all others unchanged; Redland Ranch Roses at 1,846 has no prior day to compare against). None of those 3 newly listed products matched an active (Registered or Pending) trademark name. 153 of the 156 existing cases were re-verified present in their site's current catalog feed and had their Last Verified date updated; no case content changed and no previously recorded listing disappeared. The 3 Flower Meadow Dream cases could not be checked because that domain was unreachable (see its note). Two Redland Ranch Roses products initially matched Pending chart names -- a peony ('Monsieur') and a heuchera ('Wildberry'). Neither product is a rose, so neither is a finding; per user instruction 2026-09-17 they are dropped rather than held or reported, and the crawler now discards non-rose products before matching so they do not recur.

screenshot_limitation: Still no case has a screenshot on file -- same network-proxy limitation as prior runs (headless Chromium cannot complete a connection through this environment's egress proxy). Explained to the user in chat on 2026-09-14; awaiting their choice of approach (manual capture vs. Wayback Machine vs. environment-level fix).

email_delivery.note: Report delivered as a repository link, not a PDF attachment. Two attachment attempts were built and both were rejected before sending: the first was truncated (3 of the 5 base64 chunks), the second did not match the real file on verification (its object 53 read /Length 1374 against the file's 1163 -- the later chunks had been reconstructed rather than copied). Nothing damaged was sent. The email states the reason plainly and links the committed report. See CLAUDE.md Open Items. A third attempt was made after the user asked for a fix and a re-send: the report was rebuilt at 9,221 bytes (down from 19,390) to shorten the payload, and the attachment was then checked against the source file rather than sampled at the ends. It was corrupt too -- one character wrong in the dashboard URL (...80699febeeb1 for ...80697febeeb1) -- so it was not sent and the draft was cleared. Hand-transcribed attachments are now ruled out; see CLAUDE.md Open Items.
